declared_proposition: For normalized centered quadratic CRT signs and any probability measure, product damping x_S=product_(l in S)x_l satisfies D_x=sum_(S nonempty)x_S b_S^2<=product_l(1+c_l x_l)-1, where c_l=(l-1)/(l-3)<=2. Every signed aggregate is bounded in square by [product(1+x_l)-1][product(1+c_l x_l)-1]. Thus sum x_l=o(1) forces universal saving. At critical damping x_l=tau/m, however, a nonnegative even product-tilt mixture has every singleton and odd coefficient zero while its signed aggregate tends to cosh(tau/2)-1. If the full-mode multiplier stays at least eta>0, the entropy is at least m eta^(1/m) and the coefficient norm at least 2^m sqrt(eta)-1.
mathematical_argument: The two squared values of psi_l are (l-3)/(l-1) and (l-1)/(l-3). Jensen bounds b_S^2 by E_nu psi_S^2; expanding the product gives the energy cap, and Cauchy gives the signed cap. For q=1/2, the density one-half times product(1+q psi_l) plus one-half times product(1-q psi_l) is nonnegative and normalized. Its b_S is q^|S| in even degree and zero in odd degree, proving the critical counterfamily. AM-GM gives the entropy lower bound under full-mode retention, while 1+x>=2 sqrt(x) gives the exponential norm lower bound.

reproducible_computation.no_go_scope: The counterfamily is a nonnegative CRT probability model, not actual prime weights. The theorem closes only product damping based on entropy and local centering. Nonproduct kernels, genuine prime-weighted Type-II cancellation, a parity-retaining transfer, and positive twin principal mass remain open.
